headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors if pdf.js outputs are fed into pipecat’s shared-bus, third-party-connected pipelines; prompt injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and can run in browser-based tests, while pipecat commonly consumes text/conversation state over a shared bus. A direct injection path is not documented, but if pdf.js output is manually or programmatically bridged into pipecat, malicious PDF text could influence downstream prompts. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this stays low.
conditions: IF pdf.js-rendered text is copied into pipecat prompts or memory without sanitization
IF a shared bus or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection scrubber before passing PDF text to pipecat
Keep the agents on separate workspaces and avoid shared clipboard use
Require explicit human review of extracted PDF text before LLM ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all pdf.js-derived content

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and file inputs, while pipecat touches text, conversation state, and can call many external APIs with allowlisted egress. If the same documents or extracted text flow from pdf.js into pipecat, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through pipecat’s third-party services. This is a default-path concern for pipecat integrations, though not proven for this exact pair.
conditions: IF PDF content processed by pdf.js is forwarded into any pipecat LLM/STT/TTS API service
IF the shared workspace contains sensitive PDFs and pipecat reads them
mitigations: Disable external API services in pipecat for sensitive jobs
Use a redaction step before handing text from pdf.js to pipecat
Separate local PDF processing from networked speech pipelines
Review pipecat service configuration for unintended egress
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes PDF files, while pipecat supports multiple instances with shared-bus session state and broad API integrations. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable state, they can overwrite or race on artifacts and session data. The conflict is plausible in default deployments that reuse directories or buses, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared bus
IF pipecat session state and pdf.js artifacts are updated concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Avoid sharing mutable session state between instances
Check for collisions in filenames and conversation IDs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document text, and pipecat can route that text into LLM, memory, or transport services. If pipecat treats pdf.js output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors or hallucinated interpretations can cascade into downstream actions or responses. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits with uncertainty escalated.
conditions: IF pipecat uses pdf.js-extracted text as authoritative input
IF downstream pipecat services act on that text without verification
mitigations: Require a verification step before downstream action
Keep extracted text separate from validated facts
Add citation or source-link checks in the pipeline
Log and review mismatches between source PDF and extracted text
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js is open-source and local-file oriented, while pipecat can send text and conversation state to multiple external services. The main compliance issue is a policy mismatch if regulated PDF content is routed from pdf.js into pipecat’s networked services. No specific residency or certification conflict is documented for this pair, so the risk is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated PDF content is processed by pdf.js and then sent through pipecat to external APIs
IF organizational policy forbids third-party processing of the touched data class
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of networked pipecat flows
Document a data-handling policy for PDF-derived text
Disable analytics and external service integrations for sensitive runs
Confirm retention settings for each pipecat provider
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
